title: Heit el-Ghurab, the "Lost City of the Pyramids" (Giza)
summary: Heit el-Ghurab is a Fourth Dynasty settlement on the Giza Plateau, about 400 m south of the Sphinx. Its bakeries, workshops, barracks and a royal grain store served the pyramid projects of Khafre and Menkaure. The Ancient Egypt Research Associates have dug it since 1988.

uncertainty.note: Sources give c. 2600 BC and the 4th Dynasty; the end year is a rounded bound since AERA says it was decommissioned after Menkaure's pyramid was completed. No reign years were opened.

where.modern_name: Heit el-Ghurab ("Wall of the Crow"), Giza Plateau, Egypt (pin is the Giza pyramid complex, not the site itself)
where.historical_name: Workers' and administrative town south of the Giza pyramids, Fourth Dynasty Old Kingdom Egypt

importance.justification: The best-documented town of pyramid-building workers and administrators, central to how Giza was staffed and supplied.
